shared: Edit image 1, the existing technical diagram, using image 2 ONLY as a rendering-style reference. Preserve image 1's scientific meaning, exact numbers, equations, arrow directions, panel letters and subject. Improve it into a rich academic engineering diagram: white canvas, softly tinted blue, grey, ochre, rose and green sections, thin colored outlines, nested mini-panels, clearly rendered math, compact tables, small flat schematic icons, aligned grids and precise connectors, like MATLAB/Simulink figures. Use a restrained scientific sans-serif font, legible labels and edge-safe margins. Image 2's appeal is its detailed colored technical structure; do NOT copy its branding, giant header, decorative border or thumbnail layout. No NVIDIA logo, CUDA logo, company mark, NVIDIA word, CUDA word, WINDWEAVE title, certificate, seal, slogan, watermark, neon, photorealistic processors or futuristic scenery. No invented data, benchmark, date, performance curve, hardware specification or numerical result. Add richness through geometry and structured subpanels, not more unsupported claims. Keep the source's wide landscape proportions. Keep all labels in English and mathematics typeset cleanly. Make a full standalone figure, not a cover. Correct source details below take precedence if a visual simplification is ambiguous.

figures.name: architecture
figures.prompt: Figure: CPU–GPU streaming architecture. Preserve two panels a and b. Panel a has five connected groups in order: ERA5 archive (location CSVs) → Sample address (i maps to file j and start a) → CPU worker (slice + normalize) → Prefetch / collate (W workers, P prefetched batches per worker) → GPU step (forward / backward). Add nested source-table, compact cumulative-index, normalized sequence-matrix, queued mini-batch and generic model-network graphics to these groups. Show ordinary transfer of tensors, without claiming custom CUDA streams or asynchronous transfer. Panel b is lifecycle: Index {N_j,C_j} → Normalize (n,mu,M2) to (mu,sigma) → Construct (X_enc,T_enc,X_dec,T_dec,Y) → Consume loss or reward to gradient. Index and statistics happen at initialization; construction and consumption repeat during training. Use five distinct quiet panel colors, aligned arrows, small stack/table sketches, and a clearly separate initialization/repetition band. Keep the panel headers 'Streaming data path' and 'Training lifecycle and retained state'. Input observations are archived, not a live weather feed. No additional numerical statistics.

figures.name: index
figures.prompt: Figure: implicit window indexing. Preserve panels a, b and c, and the EXACT worked example. File A has 99 rows and 4 windows, global indices 0,1,2,3. File B has 117 rows and 6 windows, global indices 4,5,6,7,8,9. Cumulative counts C=[4,10]. Highlight index i=6. Resolve: j=bisect_right([4,10],6)=1; ell=6-C_0=2; a=ell*s=2*9=18. Selected rows in file B are the half-open interval [18,90): encoder [18,63) is 45 rows, target [63,90) is 27 rows. Timeline row ticks are exactly 0,18,63,90,117, with blue encoder and rose target. Row lengths L=45, H=27, stride s=9. Add a small two-row source metadata table and subtle arrows linking the selected global index, file B and highlighted row interval. Use colored file/window tiles and layered address-resolution cards. Do not change any number, end interval, strict cumulative comparison or zero-based index. Do not add invented archive file counts or years.

figures.name: normalization
figures.prompt: Figure: parallel normalization by sufficient statistics. Preserve panel a: three independent file grids A (blue), B (rose), C (grey), each returning a compact summary (n_j,mu_j,M2_j); arrows converge into one Merge node (n,mu,M2); then sigma=sqrt(M2/n). Show a tiny table/grid inside each file and a separate summary card, then a restrained green reducer output. Panel b is an EXACT toy example: file A values [0,2], mu_A=1, n_A=2, M2_A=2; file B values [4,6], mu_B=5, n_B=2, M2_B=2. Merged mu=3, n=4, M2=2+2+4^2*(2*2/4)=20. Keep this formula exactly, rendered cleanly. Use a common horizontal scale for the blue and rose point pairs, subtle vertical mean markers and a highlighted between-file correction card to explain why the variation is retained. Label 'Exact toy values' once. No weather measurements or empirical distributions. Preserve headings 'Parallel summary reduction' and 'Between-file correction'.

figures.name: tensors
figures.prompt: Figure: encoder–decoder tensor alignment. Preserve two panels a Observation alignment and b Five tensors returned per sample. In panel a, encoder history covers rows [0,45), future target covers [45,72), and gold outline highlights known decoder context [21,45) of length K=24. Ticks EXACTLY 0,21,45,72. L=45 and H=27. In panel b, five aligned tensor cards in order: X_enc,45×4,Float32,blue; T_enc,45×4,Int64,grey; X_dec,51×4,Float32,gold known values plus outlined zeros; T_dec,51×4,Int64,grey; Y,27×2,Float32,rose. X_dec consists of 24 observed context rows followed by 27 zero-placeholder rows; do not put future observed values into it. Future time marks are known, future feature values are hidden. Add a thin line from the highlighted historical context to the gold decoder region, and from future timestamps to T_dec, showing alignment without suggesting observed future values enter the model. Matrices can be compressed schematics, but shape labels and data types must be exact. Use a small zero-placeholder legend and a compact source-row strip for richness. No spatial CNN dimensions, (C,H,W), heatmap dataset counts, or unnecessary batch axes.

figures.name: locality
figures.prompt: Figure: worker-local cache behavior and prefetch payload. Preserve all three panels a Local file access, b Interleaved file access, c Queued tensor payload. Panel a requests A,A,A,A,B,B; results read,reuse,reuse,reuse,read,reuse. Panel b requests A,B,C,A,C,B; results read,read,read,read,read,read. Show one active DataFrame per worker with file-colored table tiles and a clear cache-hit/replacement schematic. Panel c is an analytical line plot; preserve its geometry and values from image 1 faithfully. Horizontal axis Worker count W is 1..16 with ticks 1,4,8,12,16; vertical Raw tensor payload (MiB) is 0..10 with ticks 0,2,4,6,8,10. Three straight lines for P=1 (blue), P=2 (ochre), P=4 (rose), all computed from M=WPBS, B=32, S=4824 bytes, converted to MiB by division by 1048576. At W=16 the endpoints are approximately 2.36,4.71,9.42 MiB. Preserve line ordering and do not draw an empirical curve. Keep the short caption 'Analytical estimate; excludes file caches'. Enhance the frame and grouped panels, legend, thin scientific grid and small batch-stack graphic, without changing chart scales. Do not invent measured throughput or RAM savings.

figures.name: sequence
figures.prompt: Figure: batch-production sequence. Preserve two panels. Panel a has four lifelines in this order: Training loop, DataLoader, CPU worker, CSV/cache. Messages descend in this exact order and direction: Training loop → DataLoader request batch; DataLoader → CPU worker assign indices; CPU worker → CSV/cache read on miss; CSV/cache → CPU worker active DataFrame; CPU worker → DataLoader five aligned tensors; DataLoader → Training loop collated batch. Use colored actor headings with small flat process/file/table icons and thin dashed lifelines, precisely aligned message labels and return arrows. A worker-local cache, not a shared or autonomous scheduler, is depicted. Panel b shows CPU batch1,batch2,batch3,batch4 prepared in order, and GPU batch1,batch2,batch3,batch4 with the same order shifted later. This is a schematic of preparation ahead of GPU demand, not measured timing or copy/compute overlap. Use blue CPU strips and rose GPU strips, with a light queue-gap annotation and generic ordering arrow. Keep the note 'ordering only; widths do not represent measured durations'. No timing units, asynchronous transfer claim, fabricated latency or utilization.

figures.name: feedback
figures.prompt: Figure: forecast–reward learning loop. Preserve panels a History and withheld future, b Optimization routes using the same streamed sample. Panel a uses a blue history segment [0,45), rose withheld future [45,72), ticks 0,45,72; S contains 45 history rows and time marks, Y contains 27 target rows; a next-window arrow shows streaming continues. Panel b contains two separate routes from the SAME streamed sample. Blue supervised: forecast → L_MSE(prediction,Y) → backpropagate. Ochre RL policy: sample forecast → R(prediction,Y) → policy gradient, with a feedback loop returning to forecast sampling probabilities. Make it a rich learning diagram with small encoder/Informer blocks, blue/rose target matrices, a compact stochastic sampling graphic, and a four-cell reward-component strip labeled component error, temporal pattern, event agreement, variability. All charts, if added, must be distribution sketches without numerical results. Preserve the mathematical symbols and distinguish MSE backpropagation from policy-gradient optimization. Historical future observations provide offline feedback; there is no live physical environment transition. Do not add learning curves, accuracy bars, convergence claims, 24% result, brand marks, or completed-training claims.
